record.question: State True or False: (b) Any errors in Annual Statement of GPF Accounts should be brought to the notice of the Accounts Officer within three months from the date of receipt of statement.
record.explanation: True. GPF Rule 39(2) requires errors in the annual statement to be reported to the Accounts Officer within three months after receipt; the source paper wording was checked on page 3 (https://indiankanoon.org/doc/26699763/).

record.question: State True or False: (c) Nomination made by the subscriber while in service can be changed even after retirement so long as the amount remains unpaid.
record.explanation: True. The Comptroller and Auditor General Accountant General (A&E) FAQ confirms a subscriber can change a GPF nomination after retirement until the balance is drawn. The proposal that this statement was false is incorrect. Source paper wording checked on page 3 (https://cag.gov.in/ae/allahabad/en/faqs?type=gpf).

record.question: State True or False: (d) Portion of the money misappropriated by the official can be made good from his GPF.
record.explanation: False. GPF money cannot be used to make good money misappropriated by the official; the Government of India ruling is reproduced in CAG materials (https://cag.gov.in/uploads/media/Final-Annual-Review-2023-24-0682d76bb16df94-53306870.pdf). Source paper wording checked on page 3.

record.question: State True or False: (a) When the subscriber leaves no family, if a nomination made by him in accordance with provisions of Rule 5 in favour of any person or persons subsists, the amount standing to his credit in the fund to which the nomination relates, shall become payable to his nominee or nominees.
record.explanation: True. The source statement says a valid Rule 5 nomination subsisting when the subscriber dies without family is payable to the nominee(s); the source paper wording was checked on page 3. See GPF Rule 5 and the Accountant General guidance (https://cag.gov.in/ae/allahabad/en/faqs?type=gpf).

record.question: State True or False: (e) When a subscriber quits service, the amount standing to his credit in the fund shall become payable to him.
record.explanation: True. On quitting service, final withdrawal of the GPF accumulation becomes payable subject to the rules. The Accountant General FAQ lists retirement, dismissal, resignation, compulsory retirement and removal among quit-service cases (https://cag.gov.in/ae/allahabad/en/faqs?type=gpf). Source paper wording checked on page 3.
